office_does: A State Representative writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital and transportation budgets, covering school funding, tax structure, housing rules, health funding and criminal-justice statutes.
race_blurb: Republican Rep. Peter Abbarno of Chehalis, a Centralia attorney and House Republican Caucus chair, seeks a fourth term against Democrat Andy Zahn, a Toutle writer and photographer in his first race. They split on taxes, data centers and AI, corporate campaign money and climate policy.

candidates.summary: State representative since 2021, former Centralia City Council member and Centralia attorney, running on tax relief, affordability and bringing capital-budget money to the district.
highlights: Voted no on the 2026 tax on income over $1 million and the 2025 tax package; pledges 'meaningful tax relief' [S5][S6][S1]
Says he helped secure $81 million in 2025 capital-budget money for the district [S15]
Voted no on 2025 rent-increase limits and the clean-fuels expansion [S8][S11]
Voted no on both 2025 bills amending the parents' rights law [S9][S10]
Chairs Cascade PAC, which funds Republican candidates [S17]

taxes.basis: Voted no on ESSB 6346 and ESSB 5814, calls the income tax 'unconstitutional, unpopular, and unnecessary,' and campaigns on tax relief.

spending.basis: Voted against the 2025-27 operating budget and says taxpayers should spend their own money, while touting capital-budget money won for the district.

housing.basis: Voted against the 2025 rent-increase limits (EHB 1217); no other housing statements.

safety.basis: Backs more law-enforcement funding and stronger penalties for repeat offenders, opposed 2021 police-reform bills, and voted no on the 2026 officer face-covering bill.

climate.basis: Voted against the 2025 clean-fuels changes and called 2021 climate bills including cap-and-trade job-killing, while offering amendments to redirect rather than end the program.

parental-rights.basis: Voted against ESHB 1296 and ESSB 5181, which amended the parents' rights law; lists the right 'to parent' among rights he defends.

reform.basis: Chairs Cascade PAC, which funds Republican candidates, and accepts corporate contributions.

experience.basis: House member since 2021, House Republican Caucus chair, and six years on the Centralia City Council.

candidates.summary: Toutle freelance writer and photographer in his first race for office, running on rural parks, industrial hemp, passenger rail and limits on data centers, and refusing corporate contributions.
highlights: Proposes a moratorium on new data centers and limits on generative AI in the state [S5][S4]
Calls the state tax structure regressive and wants more revenue with less burden on middle and lower earners [S6]
Proposes publicly owned hourly passenger rail on the I-5 corridor with small-town stops [S7]
Supports a universal government-paid health care system [S6]

taxes.basis: Calls the tax structure 'deeply flawed and regressive' and says reform could raise more revenue while easing the burden on middle and lower earners; names no specific tax.

spending.basis: Proposes borrowing for self-repaying public investment in parks, rail, housing and community colleges, while saying he wants a balanced budget.

housing.basis: Proposes a publicly built rent-to-own housing model and affordable housing in town centers instead of sprawl.

climate.basis: Says fossil-fuel extraction and use must cease and calls climate change urgent; prioritizes demand reduction and distributed solar.

healthcare.basis: Says paying for health care through a government universal health care system would save individuals 'an immense amount of money.'

tech.basis: Repeatedly calls for a data-center moratorium, a ban on generative AI and cryptocurrency in data centers, higher data-center utility taxes and AI-content labeling.

reform.basis: Says big-money interests must be evicted from government and has vowed to refuse all corporate contributions.

experience.basis: First bid for any elected office, with no elected experience.
